question: Can the shared hand anchor depend on reticle input, and can reach compression add shoulder motion with fixed head/controller/yaw and no clamping?
claim: On the native +0x17EC reticle-input branch, RVA 0x1585320 writes a screen-dependent unprojected point to ArkPlayer+0x17D4, not camera-centre translation. PreyVR copies that field into GameplayPoseFrame.nativeEye and adds it to both hand goals; reticle follow supplies an aim-dependent producer input. Separately ScaleReach contributes (1-k) of shoulder movement. Fixed-input compiled math reproduces both dependencies without a camera-yaw change or clamping. Their runtime magnitudes and share of the reported wearer symptom are unresolved.
method: Read handover and source pinned at 087d3be09dfb209cf9cc260062192ce009241864. Use current-session read-only Ghidra decompile_function/disassemble_function/read_memory/get_program_options on /Prey/PreyDll.dll; imported SHA from Program Information matches installed PE hash. Python 3.12 pefile compared all 2230 producer bytes at RVA 0x1585320 with Ghidra data. Build the evidence-directory CMake harness with MSVC 19.50.35729.0 against exact snapshots of AnimIk, StereoCamera and VrMath. The near-plane input is an analytical projection fixture, not native emulation. Original handover, decompile, assembly, bytes, source excerpts, fixture and exact build/run output are retained.

do_not_repeat.approach: Interpret zero clamping or zero right-target writes as eliminating all additive coupling into the left goal.
do_not_repeat.reason: Reach compression includes current animated shoulder motion even while unclamped, and the shared ray anchor does not require a right-target write.

next_action: Runtime owner should isolate aim.reticle field writes while preserving aim.enable and healthy left IK, then compare reach 65/100 with both unclamped. Keep rotation-only and translation-only right-hand sweeps separate. Implement independent cyclops/head, native-ray and firing-origin contracts; do not blind-read the live stereo camera. Consider a contribution to existing playbook origin/feedback guidance with this scoped example, not a new universal prohibition or claimed headset fix.
